answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to host a timed summit of peer verification that consumes a unique relic of prior epoch state while emitting a one-time whisper of fresh entropy. The summit demands simultaneous multi-agent computation on that relic, so an attacker must provision distinct hardware instances and real-time coordination bandwidth for every fake identity; cheap clones share the same resources and fail the concurrent check, making large-scale sybil farms economically prohibitive.
